title: Ohio household-cost standard: 2025 methods
description: Editable source-backed budget definitions and household assumptions for the 2025 Self-Sufficiency Standard.
dataPeriod: 2025 methodological edition; individual input years retained in source notes
geography: Ohio household-cost production; national model with state and county inputs
methodology: Each row records a source method or interpretation, not a count of households. Text is paraphrased from the full 2025 CWW Technical Brief; the unchanged public-reader extraction and original retained PDF remain linked. Original 2026 report Tables 4 and 5 OCR is retained separately for editorial comparison. County monetary amounts belong to the separate Ohio 2025 workbook.

values.label: Model scope
values.included: Full basic-needs costs without public subsidies or informal/private help.
values.interpretation: Costs vary by county and household composition; the assumptions describe working-age adults working full time.

rows.note: Method definition; original publisher text and report comparison retained.

values.label: Work and time units
values.included: Eight hours per day, 22 days per month and 12 months per year; 176 hours in the standard work month.
values.interpretation: Keep the source's hourly-per-worker, monthly-household and annual-household labels with their original values.

rows.locator: 2025 Technical Brief, printed pages 4–5; original report Table 5
rows.note: Method definition; original publisher text and report comparison retained.

values.label: Working adults
values.included: One- and two-adult households assume all adults work full time year-round. Additional adults beyond two are non-working dependants.
values.interpretation: Additional adults contribute housing, food, health and miscellaneous costs; transportation costs are assigned to the working adults.

rows.note: Method definition; original publisher text and report comparison retained.

values.label: Child age groups
values.interpretation: Select actual source household counts and ages together when comparing county costs.

rows.note: Method definition; original publisher text and report comparison retained.

values.label: Housing
values.included: HUD fair-market rent and utilities; bedroom requirements follow household size.
values.interpretation: Use the original county housing amount; telephone/broadband costs are recorded with miscellaneous costs.

rows.note: Method definition; original publisher text and report comparison retained.

values.label: Child care
values.included: Weighted home and centre care: infants 43%/57%, preschool 26%/74%, school age 46%/54%.
values.interpretation: Infants and preschool children receive full-time care; school-age care is part time in the school year and full time in summer.

rows.note: Method definition; original publisher text and report comparison retained.

values.label: Food
values.included: Groceries using the USDA Low-Cost Food Plan, June 2024 costs, adjusted by county.
values.interpretation: The 2025 method cites the 2024 Map the Meal Gap release using 2022 data for its county food-cost index. Keep that input period separate from newer food-insecurity estimates.

rows.note: Method definition; original publisher text and report comparison retained.

values.label: Transportation
values.included: Local transit for qualifying areas, or ownership and running costs of a car for each of the first two working adults.
values.interpretation: Includes commuting, child-care stops and an errand trip; the model does not add the initial purchase price of the vehicle.

rows.note: Method definition; original publisher text and report comparison retained.

values.label: Health care
values.included: Employer-sponsored insurance contributions and age-specific out-of-pocket costs.
values.interpretation: The 2025 update uses MEPS metropolitan/non-metropolitan premiums and single, employee-plus-one or family coverage by household size.

rows.note: Method definition; original publisher text and report comparison retained.

values.label: Miscellaneous
values.included: Other necessities allowance plus broadband, equipment and mobile phone/service costs.
values.interpretation: The 2025 broadband specification is 100 Mbps down/20 Mbps up. Mobile service is modelled for each adult. Keep all these costs within the source category.

rows.note: Method definition; original publisher text and report comparison retained.

values.label: Taxes and credits
values.included: The source calculates federal/state income taxes, payroll and relevant sales taxes, with applicable tax credits.
values.interpretation: Credits are displayed as monthly amounts in the model. Preserve whether the workbook tax field is gross or net of credits before summing a budget.

rows.locator: 2025 Technical Brief, printed pages 22–25; original report Table 5 note
rows.note: Method definition; original publisher text and report comparison retained.

values.label: Basic-needs scope
values.included: The basic standard covers daily needs under its working-family assumptions.
values.interpretation: The method does not estimate additional costs of retirement or a work-limiting disability. Savings, education and debt repayment require their own interpretation.

rows.note: Method definition; original publisher text and report comparison retained.

values.label: Emergency savings
values.included: A separate calculation covers one adult's income loss over an average unemployment spell, after expected unemployment benefits.
values.interpretation: For two-adult households the second adult remains employed. Keep the emergency-savings supplement separate from the basic monthly and annual standard.

rows.note: Method definition; original publisher text and report comparison retained.
